name: Peter Pan's Flight
sensoryNotes: Suspended pirate galleons flying through dark rooms illuminated with glowing UV blacklight scenery. Gentle flight motion.
adhdTip: Continuous moving boarding belt. Very popular queue; aim for early rope drop or during evening fireworks.

name: Big Thunder Mountain
sensoryNotes: Fast-paced runaway mine train over water and through pitch-black tunnels. Loud lift chains, whistles, and abrupt drops.
adhdTip: The underwater return tunnel is pitch dark and very noisy. Ear defenders recommended for sound-sensitive kids.

name: Phantom Manor
sensoryNotes: Slow-moving continuous doom buggies through dark rooms featuring ghosts, skeletons, thunder, lightning, and eerie orchestral music.
adhdTip: The pre-show stretching room plunges into complete darkness with a sudden scream and thunderclap. Prepare nervous children in advance.

name: Pirates of the Caribbean
sensoryNotes: Indoor boat cruise through dim pirate caverns with two unexpected short drops in the dark. Cannon fire, splashing water, and battle effects.
adhdTip: The queue line is long, winding, and dimly lit underground. Sitting in the front row may result in light water spray during drops.

name: Star Wars Hyperspace Mountain
sensoryNotes: High-speed indoor roller coaster with catapult launch, 3 inversions, flashing laser projections, and loud Star Wars orchestral audio.
adhdTip: Very intense sensory immersion with rapid flashing lights in pitch darkness. Not recommended for children prone to sensory overload.

name: Buzz Lightyear Laser Blast
sensoryNotes: Interactive spinning omnimover equipped with laser blasters. Bright neon colors, constant electronic sound effects, and guest-controlled vehicle spinning.
adhdTip: Great for active kids who like gamified tasks. Riders have full joystick control over spinning the cart 360 degrees.

name: 'it's a small world'
sensoryNotes: Gentle, brightly lit canal boat ride through singing doll dioramas. Repetitive melodic soundtrack and vibrant pastel visuals.
adhdTip: A calming, low-sensory reset ride during busy afternoons. The continuous queue moves steadily with plenty of visual stimulation.

name: Star Tours: The Adventures Continue
sensoryNotes: 3D motion simulator cabin with hydraulic pitching, sudden drops, and synchronized space combat visuals.
adhdTip: Requires 3D glasses. Guests sensitive to motion sickness or enclosed spaces should focus on the fixed cabin frame during flight.

name: Indiana Jones and the Temple of Peril
sensoryNotes: Outdoor looping coaster with rapid sharp turns, sudden drops, and a quick 360-degree inversion.
adhdTip: High physical restraint pressure with moderate head rattling on turns. Strict 140cm height limit enforced.

name: Dumbo the Flying Elephant
sensoryNotes: Gentle outdoor circular aerial carousel with lever-controlled height adjustment.
adhdTip: Unshaded outdoor queue line can feel slow. Letting the child control the elevation lever gives great engagement and autonomy.

name: Mad Hatter's Tea Cups
sensoryNotes: Spinning teacups under a stained-glass pavilion. Center wheel allows riders to spin mildly or fast.
adhdTip: If spinning triggers vestibular overwhelm, leave the wheel untouched for a gentle gliding motion.

name: Casey Jr. – Le Petit Train du Cirque
sensoryNotes: Fast-paced mini coaster through fairytale storybook miniature landscapes with cheerful circus tunes.
adhdTip: Ask Cast Members for open-air sleigh cars if your child prefers open space rather than the enclosed circus cage carts.

name: Le Pays des Contes de Fées
sensoryNotes: Quiet, gentle outdoor canal boat through miniature handcrafted Disney fairytale villages.
adhdTip: One of the best de-escalation rides in the resort. Peaceful with no sudden movements or loud sounds.

name: Blanche-Neige et les Sept Nains
sensoryNotes: Dark ride in mine carts encountering the Evil Queen, transformation mirrors, and the haunted forest.
adhdTip: Despite the fairytale theme, recurring witch pop-outs and dark woodland can scare sensitive or young children.

name: Les Voyages de Pinocchio
sensoryNotes: Traditional dark ride following Pinocchio with Stromboli's cage, Pleasure Island, and Monstro the whale.
adhdTip: Fast scene transitions with loud shouting dialogue from Stromboli. Reassure kids of the happy ending with the Blue Fairy.

name: Autopia
sensoryNotes: Gasoline-powered go-kart circuit along guided rails with real accelerator pedal and steering.
adhdTip: Engine vibrations and petrol fumes present. Steering wheels pull abruptly when bouncing against center guide rails.

name: Orbitron
sensoryNotes: Elevated spinning retro-futuristic rocket ships with high panoramic views over Discoveryland.
adhdTip: Rockets bank outward and travel higher than Dumbo. Very slow load/unload cycle so queues move slowly.

name: Le Carrousel de Lancelot
sensoryNotes: Grand ornate carousel with moving wooden horses and organ pipe music.
adhdTip: Stationary chariot benches are available on the inner ring for children who dislike the vertical bouncing motion.

name: Disneyland Railroad
sensoryNotes: Scenic steam train circling the perimeter of Disneyland Park with dioramas of the Grand Canyon.
adhdTip: Useful transport to rest tired legs between Main Street, Frontierland, Fantasyland, and Discoveryland.

name: Thunder Mesa Riverboat Landing
sensoryNotes: Authentic paddle steamer cruise around Big Thunder Mountain and Wilderness Island with steam whistle sounds.
adhdTip: Plenty of open deck space allowing children to walk around freely during the 15-minute sailing.

name: Main Street Vehicles & Horse-Drawn Streetcars
sensoryNotes: Vintage fire trucks, paddy wagons, omnibuses, and horse-drawn trolleys traversing Town Square to Central Plaza.
adhdTip: Operates during morning and early afternoon. Low-stress scenic ride.

name: Rustler Roundup Shootin' Gallery
sensoryNotes: Laser-activated frontier target range with animated props, cawing crows, and western piano tunes.
adhdTip: Requires supplementary coin payment (€2 per round). Excellent focused manual stimulation.

name: Alice's Curious Labyrinth
sensoryNotes: Self-paced hedge maze with water fountains, singing flowers, Cheshire Cat animatronics, and Queen of Hearts Castle tower.
adhdTip: Zero waiting time and complete freedom of movement. Helpful space for kids to burn excess energy.

name: La Tanière du Dragon
sensoryNotes: Walkthrough cave under the castle housing an animatronic dragon that wakes, breathes smoke, and growls.
adhdTip: Very dark and damp environment. Children can exit directly back into the castle courtyard if overwhelmed.

name: La Galerie de la Belle au Bois Dormant
sensoryNotes: Upper-floor castle gallery with stained glass windows, illustrated storybooks, and tapestries.
adhdTip: Offers a tranquil indoor vantage point overlooking Fantasyland when park pathways become crowded.

name: La Cabane des Robinson
sensoryNotes: Elevated treehouse staircase climb with shipwreck architecture and waterwheel systems.
adhdTip: Requires lots of stairs. Good physical outlet for energetic kids, but not pushchair or wheelchair accessible.

name: Adventure Isle & Pirate Galleon
sensoryNotes: Outdoor island with suspension bridges, rocky labyrinths, skull caves, and pirate ship exploration.
adhdTip: Unstructured exploration zone with secret pathways and bouncy bridges.

name: Les Mystères du Nautilus
sensoryNotes: Walkthrough submarine with steampunk props, glowing organ pipes, and an encounter with an animatronic squid outside the porthole.
adhdTip: Self-paced, cool, and air-conditioned during hot summer days with low crowd density.

name: Liberty Arcade & Discovery Arcade
sensoryNotes: Covered architectural walkways running parallel behind Main Street shops with gaslit lanterns, vintage models, and historical dioramas.
adhdTip: Useful quiet bypass to escape parade crowds, inclement weather, and open street congestion.

name: Meet Mickey Mouse
sensoryNotes: Indoor backstage magician dressing room where families meet Mickey Mouse 1-on-1 for photos and autographs.
adhdTip: Queue plays classic Mickey cartoons on screens to keep children engaged while waiting.

name: Princess Pavilion
sensoryNotes: Intimate stone palace meeting room with dynamic crystal lighting and 1-on-1 Disney Princess interactions.
adhdTip: Can have long queue times. Use Lineberty or visit early morning to minimize wait.

name: The Lion King: Rhythms of the Pride Lands
sensoryNotes: Indoor acrobatic musical in Frontierland Theater. Live tribal drumming, high-wire gymnastics, singers, and dynamic stage lighting.
adhdTip: High-decibel live drumming and singing. Sitting further back from the stage softens the acoustic impact.

name: Disney Stars on Parade
sensoryNotes: Daytime musical parade with mechanical floats, dancers, and a fire-breathing Maleficent steampunk dragon.
adhdTip: Main Street curbs fill up 45 minutes early. Stand near 'it's a small world' gates for easier post-parade exit.

name: Disney Tales of Magic Nighttime Spectacular
sensoryNotes: Castle projection mapping, synchronized drone swarms, laser arrays, water fountains, and fireworks.
adhdTip: Sudden loud firework booms and dense crowd density on Central Plaza. Ear defenders strongly advised.

name: Crush's Coaster
sensoryNotes: Spinning turtle shell roller coaster inside the dark East Australian Current. Unpredictable gravity spins, drops, and jellyfish projections.
adhdTip: Consistently long wait times. Use Single Rider line or Premier Access to manage queue duration.

name: Ratatouille: The Adventure
sensoryNotes: Trackless 3D rat vehicles across giant kitchen floors. Heat blast effects from ovens, water mists, and mop chases.
adhdTip: Smooth trackless motion. If 3D glasses cause visual fatigue, the ride can still be experienced comfortably without them.

name: The Twilight Zone Tower of Terror
sensoryNotes: Haunted hotel service elevator with multiple randomized rapid vertical freefall drops and upward launches. Stomach-floating weightlessness.
adhdTip: Intense physical and psychological drop sensations. Prepare children who are cautious around heights or sudden falling motions.

name: Avengers Assemble: Flight Force
sensoryNotes: Catapult launch roller coaster (0-60mph in 2.8s) with 3 inversions in near pitch-black space alongside Iron Man & Captain Marvel audio/visual screens.
adhdTip: High acceleration G-force launch with over-the-shoulder restraints. Keep head firmly back against headrest.

name: Spider-Man W.E.B. Adventure
sensoryNotes: Interactive 3D mission using gesture-recognition camera technology where riders sling virtual webs with their hands to catch Spider-Bots.
adhdTip: Active physical arm movements. Suitable for kids with high energy who enjoy gamified attractions.

name: RC Racer
sensoryNotes: Orange half-pipe steel shuttle coaster racing 25 meters up and down with intense vertical drop sensations.
adhdTip: Higher rows experience intense weightlessness at the top of the spikes. Choose middle rows for milder thrills.

name: Toy Soldiers Parachute Drop
sensoryNotes: Outdoor tower parachute drops with mild drop sensations and high panoramic views of the park.
adhdTip: Helpful intermediate ride for kids building confidence toward Tower of Terror.

name: Slinky Dog Zigzag Spin
sensoryNotes: Gentle circular undulating ride following Slinky Dog chasing his tail around a dog bowl.
adhdTip: Mild and smooth motion. Suitable as a starter ride for toddlers and sensory-sensitive visitors in Toy Story Playland.

name: Cars ROAD TRIP
sensoryNotes: Scenic open-air tram tour culminating at 'Cars-tastrophe Canyon' with an earthquake simulation, fire bursts, and a water deluge.
adhdTip: Left side of the tram receives light water spray during the canyon flash flood sequence.

name: Cars Quatre Roues Rallye
sensoryNotes: Spinning cars on criss-crossing rotating turntables in Radiator Springs.
adhdTip: Smooth transition movements as cars shift between turntables.

name: Hero Training Center
sensoryNotes: Interactive Marvel encounter featuring dynamic multi-camera freeze-frame technology with Spider-Man, Iron Man, or Captain Marvel.
adhdTip: Virtual Queue reservation required via the official Disneyland Paris app during your park visit.

name: Frozen Ever After
sensoryNotes: Boat voyage through Arendelle to Elsa's Ice Palace with animatronics, music, and one short backwards/forward slope drop.
adhdTip: High-demand attraction. Consider Disney Premier Access or heading here at morning park opening.

name: Raiponce Tangled Spin
sensoryNotes: Family spinning boat attraction surrounded by glowing floating lanterns and Tangled instrumental melodies.
adhdTip: Scenic lakeside views across Adventure Bay with gentle motion.

name: Mickey and the Magician
sensoryNotes: Stage production in Animagique Theater featuring illusions, live musical numbers, and Disney character appearances.
adhdTip: Air-conditioned indoor seating with clear stage views across tiers. Arrive 25 minutes prior to showtime for preferred seats.

name: TOGETHER: a Pixar Musical Adventure
sensoryNotes: Theatrical production with live orchestra, stage projection mapping, dancers, bubbles, and sensory effects.
adhdTip: Live orchestral elements create varied acoustics. Fast-moving visual sequences.

name: Stitch Live!
sensoryNotes: Interactive digital show where animated Stitch engages directly with audience members.
adhdTip: Children can sit on front floor mats for direct interaction. Showtimes alternate between English and French.

name: Alice & the Queen of Hearts: Back to Wonderland
sensoryNotes: High-energy open-air stunt arena production featuring BMX riders, trampolinists, pop-rock battles, and audience voting.
adhdTip: Loud rock music and dynamic physical action. Ample open stadium bleacher seating.

name: Disney Cascade of Lights
sensoryNotes: Lakeside nighttime production featuring aquatic fountains, synchronized drones, lasers, and water projections.
adhdTip: Wide viewing areas along the Adventure Bay promenade reduce crowd congestion.
